name: Debugger Overlay
description: Breakpoints, watches, and the current line — the tools that turn a failing program into a lesson. A breakpoint pauses the command queue rather than the game, so the world stays interactive while the program is stopped and the player can look around at the state that caused the problem. Watched values are sampled at instruction boundaries rather than continuously, which is both cheaper and more honest: a value read mid-instruction is a value no line of the program ever saw. The overlay reads and never writes, so switching it on cannot change a run — the same rule the force visualiser follows, for the same reason.

inputs.name: maxBreakpoints
inputs.description: Breakpoints that may be set at once.

inputs.name: sampleAtInstructionBoundary
inputs.description: Whether watches are read between instructions rather than continuously. A mid-instruction value is one no line ever saw.

inputs.name: pauseWorldOnBreak
inputs.description: Whether hitting a breakpoint also freezes the world. False keeps the scene explorable while the program is stopped.

outputs.name: breakpoints
outputs.description: Instruction indices that will pause execution.

outputs.name: watches
outputs.description: Watched names and their last sampled values.

outputs.name: stoppedAt
outputs.description: Instruction index currently paused on, or -1.
